newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs close weak, pork bellies sharply lower.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs close weak, pork bellies sharply lower.

text.p: Both CME hog and pork belly futures remained pressured from expected larger hog runs and slaughter as temperatures warm in the corn belt, traders said.

Hogs closed 0.925 cent lower to 0.125 higher with only some lightly traded deferred contracts posting gains while February paced the loss at 75.350 cents. Pork bellies finished 1.975 to 1.475 cents lower with February off 1.775 at 78.400.

Moderating temperatures are expected to increase hog marketings into the weekend. Hogs backed up from the latest cold snap should come to market in the next few days and live prices could set back a few dollars per cwt, traders said.

Sell stops were touched off under 76.000 cents, basis nearbys, and fund liquidation was evident at times on chart signs the futures may have put a top in the market. April also broke through a trend line, traders said.

The larger runs will also lead to increased slaughtger and in turn a weaker cash pork complex. Recent strength in cash product was only attributed to the light slaughter and not active demand, they said.
"Cash pork was only being supported from smaller kills and now it (pork prices) look lower," one trader said.
Rand Financials and Cargill Investor Services sold early while Refco and Rosenthal Collins sold late, pit sources said.

The expected larger pace of slaughter and possibly weaker pork prices also weighed heavily on pork belly futures. The fresh belly market was firm the early part of the week but turned weak even with the pace of slaughter showed only a slight increase, traders said.

A bullishly construed weekly CME Out-of-Town storage report Tuesday had little effect on the market as most pit traders had already expected an out-movement last week despite most analysts projections of an in-movement, they said.
CME reported a net out movement of 194,000 lbs last week versus estimates of unchanged to in 600,000 lbs.
Rolling out of long positions in February ahead of its spot position added to pressure in the nearby, but short covering was also evident which limited losses, they said.

E.D.&F. Man bought May and sold February and March while Prudential Securities bought March and sold February. Rand Financials and ABN Chicogo Corp were on the other side of the spreads early. LFG, Rand Financials and Cargill Investor Services notably sold February early while R.J. O'Brien bought on the scale-down, pit sources said.
In hog options, liquidation continued in February with Lind-Waldock selling 72 puts and buying 80 calls. ADM Investor Services sold June 72 puts, pit sources added.
